page: Microsoft Azure FX4mds_v2 is a compute-optimized virtual machine running on Microsoft Hyper-V that offers an unusually high memory-to-core allocation. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz, it provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The configuration includes 84.0 GB of RAM, equating to 21.0 GB per vCPU, alongside a 260 MB L3 cache. Storage is supported locally by a 236 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance operates without a GPU or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded CPU capabilities driven by the high clock speed and vector instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Single-core performance achieves top-tier results in Geekbench (2262.0) and strong performance in tasks like single-threaded gzip compression (34.59 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.25 GB/sec). However, multi-core throughput remains restricted by the physical core count, posting bottom-quartile metrics in multi-core stress-ng (4441.27) and Clang software compilation benchmarks (5699.0). Uncached memory bandwidth tests also rank in the lower quartile, recording 35.98 GB/sec read and 25.58 GB/sec write throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the FX4mds_v2 presents a distinct hardware profile that pairs high single-core compute performance with an exceptionally large memory footprint and high-speed NVMe storage on a low core count. It is an effective platform for workloads bound by per-core software licensing, in-memory databases, memory-intensive batch processing, and caching tiers like Redis, which demonstrated 6.34 million operations per second. Conversely, it is poorly suited for heavily parallelized compute tasks or larger LLM inference workloads.

It includes 236 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and lacks a dedicated GPU. The instance features top-tier single-core Geekbench performance and strong single-threaded compression throughput, supported by advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions (AVX-512, AMX). However, its limited core count yields modest multi-core compilation and uncached memory bandwidth figures. By pairing high clock speeds with 21.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, the FX4mds_v2 provides a cost-effective environment for per-core licensed software, in-memory key-value stores like Redis, and memory-intensive single-threaded data tasks.
